objective: Test whether a fixed predictor improves synthetic regression error across four ordered groups.
scope: Software demonstration using synthetic exposed development data; not real research evidence.

definitions: Error means mean squared error on the supplied rows.
assumptions: This deterministic toy dataset is exposed development evidence.
exclusions: No trading, real-world efficacy, causal discovery or novel scientific result is claimed.
contract.acceptance_scope: Only the stated comparison on the specified synthetic dataset and conditions.

runtime.budget_units: Local operation credits; not provider currency or tokens

colony_briefs.formulations: Define the main question, controls and alternative formulations.
colony_briefs.mechanisms: Test scale and bias explanations; use a simpler scale check as a stepping stone.
colony_briefs.measurement: Check numerical reproduction, group consistency and what the measurements establish.
colony_briefs.falsification: Try counter-explanations, negative controls and tests that can overturn the leader.

research_questions.statement: Can a predictor pass both overall and worst-group error gates?
Does correcting the predictor's slope explain the overall error?
research_questions.transfer_test: Carry the slope hypothesis into the main question and check every group, bias alternatives and all gates.

seeds.title: Unit-slope control
seeds.mechanism: A unit slope is the simple baseline that a useful successor must improve.
seeds.counter_hypothesis: The target has a different slope, so the baseline is misspecified.
seeds.falsification_plan: Compare overall and worst-group error against registered gates.

seeds.title: Moderate slope correction
seeds.mechanism: Increase the slope partway to test whether scale mismatch explains residuals.
seeds.counter_hypothesis: Bias or group shifts could explain the apparent improvement.
seeds.falsification_plan: Inspect chronological groups and independently reproduce every residual.
